issues.detail: The Greek 'καυχημα υμων εσμεν' means 'we are your glory/boast' (subject-complement structure). The Vietnamese 'chúng tôi là sự khoe mình của anh em' translates it as 'we are the boasting of your brothers', which shifts the focus from 'glory/boast' to the act of 'boasting' itself. More importantly, the Greek 'καυχημα' is a noun meaning 'glory/boast', but the Vietnamese 'khoe mình' is often used as a verb (to boast). A more faithful rendering would be 'chúng tôi là vinh quang của anh em'.
